newsitem.title: FINLAND: MARKKA WEAKNESS MAY PROVE SHORT-TERM.
newsitem.headline: MARKKA WEAKNESS MAY PROVE SHORT-TERM.

text.p: The markka weakened by well over a penni against the German mark on Thursday on overseas selling triggered by comments from the finance minister, but local operators said the pressure was short-term.
They saw a correction further ahead.

DEM/FIM rose to over 2.99 per mark from 2.977 after Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said its 3.04 per mark central parity in ERM would be "approximately the correct one for us" when national currencies are fixed to the new euro in 1999.
"Our dealers said foreign investors started to sell markka," chief economist Tarja Heinonen at Postipankki said.
One senior forex dealer said many overseas investors would now probably unwind long-held markka positions and accept their losses, and those flows would take DEM/FIM weaker.
"I see DEM/FIM over 3.00 quite soon, perhaps already overnight," he said. "It can go well over 3.00 as long as dollar/mark remains at these levels," he said, when dollar/mark was around 1.87.
Finnish exporters would not be eager to convert foreign currency earnings as long as the dollar remained high.
"Today and tomorrow there will be further pressure towards 3.04 markka (per mark), but I believe there will be those operating in the opposite direction around 3.00," Heinonen at Postipankki said.
Jukka Lepomaki, chief analyst at Merita, said he did not believe the markka would weaken further, and that the market just trembled a little on Niinisto's comments since it was thin.

Swedish Enskilda's Helsinki-based economist Esko Torsti said the DEM/FIM spike was a slight surprise to him, and that the markka should be comfortably trading near the 2.97 per mark level where it was before Thursday's dip.

He agreed with Niinisto that ERM central parity rates -- 3.04 in DEM/FIM -- were a good assumption for conversion rates for the euro, but said the cyclical situation was supporting the markka at stronger levels right now.
"Now if ever, we are in a cyclical situation where we should be at the stronger side of the fluctuation band," he said, referring to strong ecomomic growth and healthy exports.
